issues.description: revoke_error surfaced on lookup endpoint without sanitization or capability gate despite author flagging the concern
issues.detail: All three reviewers hit this. RevokeErr is backend-supplied text that routinely contains paths, driver messages, endpoints, or credential fragments. The PR description itself asks whether this is safe and ships it anyway on a non-privileged endpoint. Either redact/truncate, gate behind sudo, or document the contract that backends must not put secrets in revoke errors.

issues.description: Rename FetchLeaseTimes to FetchLeaseInfo breaks an exported API with no compatibility alias
issues.detail: Pike and Torvalds both flag this as gratuitous churn on a public method. Out-of-tree callers and forks will break for a cosmetic rename. Keep FetchLeaseTimes as a thin deprecated wrapper around FetchLeaseInfo, or leave the name alone.

issues.description: Test coverage exercises only path; namespace_path and revoke_error are unverified
issues.detail: All three reviewers note that TestSystemBackend_leases asserts only the path field. The two new fields with security-relevant content and conditional gating logic have zero coverage. Add a child-namespace lease test asserting namespace_path, and a forced-revoke-failure test asserting revoke_error shape.

issues.description: Metrics label still reads fetch-lease-times after the function rename
issues.detail: metrics.MeasureSince keeps the literal "fetch-lease-times" key while the function is now FetchLeaseInfo. Either preserve the metric name with a comment explaining why, or rename it deliberately. Silent code-vs-telemetry mismatch confuses operators later.

issues.description: Test inconsistently mixes t.Context() with namespace.RootContext(nil) elsewhere in the same file
issues.detail: Pike and Torvalds both flag line 2450 changing to namespace.RootContext(t.Context()) while parallel touched tests keep nil. Drive-by inconsistency that adds noise to the diff. Pick one shape for test contexts and apply it uniformly.

issues.description: leaseInfoForExport contract for export-safe fields is undocumented
issues.detail: Knuth and Pike converge here: the projection function hand-copies fields with no stated invariant about which leaseEntry fields are export-safe or why. Either define an explicit ExportedLeaseInfo struct so the shape is the API, or add a literate comment enumerating the export set and the redaction rule.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a small, well-shaped patch with one real security concern and several execution-quality issues. The unanimous P1 is revoke_error being surfaced on a non-privileged endpoint without sanitization or capability gating — a concern the PR author themselves raised and did not resolve. Secondary consensus issues are a gratuitous exported-API rename without an alias, a now-stale metrics label, and shallow test coverage that only exercises one of the three new fields. Ship-blocking on revoke_error handling; the rest is cleanup before merge.
